questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Try to hit only the side of the obstacle.
Speed up before hitting the obstacle.

questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, approach it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down, keep your motorcycle straight, rise slightly off your seat, and roll on the throttle just before you hit it.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Follow other vehicles more closely than you would alone.
Brake later than you would if riding alone.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight. Your motorcycle will take longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start braking earlier, increase your distance from other vehicles, and look for larger gaps when crossing or merging into traffic.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding in Oregon?

options.text: Left to a judge to decide.

questions.explanation: Oregon law has severe mandatory penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to ride while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What can help you avoid a crash?

options.text: Don't use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Watch about five feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Use your turn signals, brake light, and correct lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and beside your vehicle. Always be ready to avoid a sudden hazard.

questions.question: How can you keep other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: To keep other drivers from trying to share your lane, ride in the center of the lane.

questions.question: At what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to ride while intoxicated.

questions.question: Where should you ride if hazards are on your left?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What should you NOT check during your pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle when turning?

options.text: Always press on the left handgrip.
Always press on the right handgrip.
Press on the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press on the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press on the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When turning, what happens to your stopping ability?

options.text: There is less traction available for stopping.
There is more traction available for stopping.
Stopping is no different than making a stop on a straightaway.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less traction available for stopping.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans to turn, some traction is used for turning. This leaves less traction available for braking.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Drivers can look directly at you and still not see you. Never assume other drivers notice you. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers notice your motorcycle?

options.text: Use your headlight at all times, even during the day.
Make eye contact with the other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight at all times, even during the day.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times while riding. This helps other drivers see your motorcycle.

questions.question: How should you swerve to avoid a hazard?

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the direction opposite of where you plan to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
questions.explanation: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to recover. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: What is the best way to wear jackets and pants while riding?

options.text: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
Should be loose and flap in the wind while you are riding.
Should only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials provide the best protection.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: The front tire provides the power for the bike, so you will lose acceleration.
The flat tire will shake the bike, making it hard to use the mirrors.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects steering. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely get off the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: What should a passenger do while riding?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with you through turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you. They should hold onto the passenger handholds, your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which is NOT considered protective clothing?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets, denim pants, and full-fingered gloves provide protection in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support your ankles instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Spotting hazards and deciding which ones to handle first.
Keeping space between you and other vehicles.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide which to handle first. Always use your headlight to be more visible. Keep space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: What happens if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: The steering will feel the same.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If steering feels heavy, pull off the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: Curved mirrors make cars look:
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors, but objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding. The wobble will likely stop on its own.
Release the throttle to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Speeding up makes wobbling worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by releasing the throttle gradually, lean forward and down, and pull off the road. Then fix the problem causing the wobble.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. How can you reduce your crash risk?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.
Find safer roads to ride on.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself as visible as possible by wearing bright clothing when riding, even during the day.
